title: 같은 '-요', 다른 뜻: 문장 끝 억양 듣고 읽기
objective: You can read a short dialogue with tone marks (↗ ↘ →) and tell each line's meaning, and choose the right tone for 네, 왜요, 그래요 and -죠.
summary: Learn how the tone at the end of a sentence turns -아요/어요 into a statement, question, suggestion, or command.
note: The arrows show the tone of the last syllable: ↗ rising, ↘ falling, → level and soft.

task.title: Read the tone, find the meaning
task.line: Use the tone marks ↗ (rising), ↘ (falling), and → (level, soft) to decide what each sentence means or which tone fits the situation.

items.text: A falling tone tells a fact.
A rising tone on the last syllable makes it a question.
A soft, level tone, often with 같이 or 우리, means "let's."
A short, firm fall tells someone to do something.
Rise when you think it's true but want to check.
End gently, without a rise, when you just noticed something.
Rising asks the person to repeat; falling means yes.
items.example: 네?↗ 다시 한 번 말해 주세요.

items.text: Rising shows surprise or interest; falling accepts or agrees.
items.example: A: 내일 쉬어요. B: 그래요?↗ 좋겠다!

items.text: A soft rise is a real question; a short flat fall can sound annoyed.

sections.heading: Reading tip: listen to the last syllable
paragraphs: In English, a question usually changes the word order (You are going → Are you going?). In Korean, 가요 stays the same, and only the tone of the last syllable changes.
Feeling matters too. A very short, flat ending can sound cold, especially in 네 and 왜요.

sections.heading: Read the dialogue: find the four meanings
paragraphs: 민수: 좋아요. 근데 오늘 오후에 비 오죠?↗
수진: 네, 온대요.↘ 우산 꼭 챙겨요.↘

exercises: Write ↗ or ↘ for each sentence: ① (You are asking.) 이 버스 시청에 가요? ② (You are telling.) 저는 다음 역에서 내려요. ③ (You didn't hear and want the person to say it again.) 네?
Statement, question, suggestion, or command? ① (to a friend) 주말에 같이 영화 봐요.→ ② (a teacher to students) 책 덮어요.↘ ③ (to a coworker) 점심 벌써 먹었어요?↗
Fill in the blank with -죠 and add a tone mark. You think the meeting is at three, but you are not sure, so you check with a coworker: 회의가 세 ____
Read and answer in English: A: 민호 씨, 내일 저녁에 시간 있어요?↗ B: 왜요.↘ (short and flat) — How might A feel? Write a friendlier reply for B in Korean.
True or False: ① A short, flat, falling 왜요↘ always sounds friendly. ② "밖에 눈이 오네요" usually ends with a gentle falling tone.
answers: ① suggestion ② command ③ question
A may feel that B is annoyed or doesn't want to talk. Friendlier reply: 네, 있어요. 왜요?↗ (or just 왜요?↗ with a soft rising tone)
